description: TON_IoT is a family of datasets for evaluating cyber security tools on Internet of Things and industrial IoT systems. It combines telemetry from IoT and IIoT sensors, such as weather and Modbus devices, operating system logs from Windows 7 and 10 and Ubuntu 14 and 18, and network traffic in pcap and Zeek formats, with labelled attacks including denial of service, distributed denial of service, ransomware and exploitation of web applications, gateways and services. It was produced at the Cyber Range and IoT Labs of UNSW Canberra by a team led by Nour Moustafa, on a testbed that links IoT, cloud and edge or fog layers; coverage is this single laboratory testbed, not a real plant. The data were published between 2019 and 2021, last updated on 2 June 2021, and are downloaded free from a university file share; academic use is free, commercial use needs the authors' approval, and users must cite eight listed papers. Caveats: the testbed is synthetic, so traffic mixes and attack rates differ from real plants, and the dataset size is not stated. For simulation it trains and tests intrusion detection for industrial control and IoT layers of infrastructure digital twins and supports resilience studies of cyber attacks on sensors. It is related to the HAI industrial control system security dataset and Edge-IIoTset records in this catalogue.
